metaDescription: Odoo Recruitment in practice: pipeline design, job board options, interview forms, CV retention and the hire handover, plus what Community leaves out.
intro: Odoo Recruitment is a pipeline, not a sourcing tool. A job position carries the department, the recruiter, the interviewers and the number of people you intend to hire. Applicants move across a kanban board towards a stage flagged as hired, at which point the record becomes an employee. The application itself is part of Odoo Community, which buyers who have been quoted for Enterprise on the strength of a hiring requirement often do not expect.

The screens are the easy part of the project. The work sits around them. Getting applications into Odoo from wherever candidates actually look for jobs. Giving a line manager a view of their own candidates without opening the whole pipeline to them. Deciding what a CV may be kept for and for how long. Making the accepted candidate arrive on the employee record with the right department, manager, job title and start date instead of being retyped.

Where Community stops is worth naming early. The referral programme, CV digitisation from a PDF, the salary package configurator and signature on the offer are Enterprise. Community gives you the pipeline, a public job page on your own website, interview forms built as surveys, refusal reasons with email templates and the funnel reports. For an employer hiring in the tens rather than the thousands each year, that is a complete process.
whoFor: Employers filling roughly five to fifty roles a year who already keep employee records in Odoo and want the accepted candidate to become an employee without a second round of data entry.
Gulf employers where nationality, quota band and visa availability decide whether an offer can be made at all, so the applicant record has to carry more than a name and an attachment.
Companies that would rather run their job board on their own Odoo website than pay per posting on a job site.
Groups with several companies or departments needing one pipeline where interviewers are restricted to the candidates assigned to them.
It is not for staffing agencies placing hundreds of people a month, where the candidate is the product and you need a searchable talent database rather than a pipeline per vacancy.
It is not for anyone expecting automatic CV scoring or a ranked shortlist, because standard Odoo does not score or rank applicants.

capabilities.title: Job positions and a pipeline you design
capabilities.body: A job position holds the department, company, recruiter, interviewers and the target number of hires, and the kanban shows new and in progress counts against that target. Stages are yours to define and can be limited to particular positions, so an intake of forty drivers does not have to run through the same six steps as a finance manager search. One stage carries the hired flag, and that flag is what closes the vacancy and drives the reporting.

capabilities.title: How applications reach the database
capabilities.body: Standard Odoo offers three routes. An email alias on the job position turns an inbound message into an applicant with the attachment kept as the CV. The website module publishes the position with an application form that creates the same record. A recruiter can also create an applicant by hand and drop a file on it. Source and medium fields attribute an application to the channel it came from, which is the only honest way to judge where the spend works.

capabilities.title: Interview forms and restricted interviewer access
capabilities.body: Interview forms are surveys attached to the job position, either sent to the candidate or filled in by the panel during the meeting, with scored questions if you want a number out of it. Interviewers sit in their own access group and see only the applicants assigned to them, which is what makes it reasonable to give a line manager a login. Meetings are booked from the applicant, so the slot lands in the interviewer's own calendar.

capabilities.title: CVs, duplicate detection and evaluation
capabilities.body: Attachments hold the CV and anything else the candidate sends. Odoo flags similar applicants on email address, phone number and LinkedIn profile, which catches the person applying to four of your vacancies in one week. Evaluation is a short rating scale rather than a score out of ten, so any real calibration between reviewers has to come from the interview form. Expected and proposed salary sit on the applicant, giving you the gap the offer has to close.

capabilities.title: From accepted to employee
capabilities.body: Refusal is a first class action with a reason and a matching email template, so no candidate is left without a reply and the reason survives into the reporting. On the other side, the accepted applicant becomes an employee in one step, carrying name, contact details, department, job position and manager across. Enterprise adds signature on the offer and contract, and a salary package configurator that is built around the Belgian localisation and needs work elsewhere.

capabilities.title: Reporting on the funnel
capabilities.body: Recruitment analysis is a pivot over applicants, so you can count by job position, stage, source, recruiter and refusal reason, and measure how long records sat before they were opened and before they were closed. This is where hiring gets managed rather than described. The figures only mean anything if refusals are recorded with a reason instead of applicants being deleted or parked in a stage nobody revisits.

setup.title: Design the stages before anything else
setup.body: Stages are the whole model. Decide how many you need, which are shared across every vacancy and which belong to one hiring pattern, and which single stage carries the hired flag. Four to six is usually right. Every extra stage is a drag on the recruiter who has to move records through it, and a stage that means nothing to the business produces a report nobody believes. Write down the definition of each stage before it is configured.

setup.title: The alias, the domain and mail that actually arrives
setup.body: Applications by email depend on a catchall domain that resolves, an incoming mail server Odoo can poll or a route that delivers into it, and an alias per job position. Get this working in the first week of the build rather than the week before go live, because it usually touches the client's DNS and mail provider. Test with a real attachment, from an external address, against a closed position as well as an open one.

setup.title: Access rights, and who is allowed to see a salary
setup.body: Three levels matter. An officer works the vacancies they are responsible for, an administrator sees everything and configures stages, and an interviewer sees only the candidates assigned to them. Decide early whether expected and proposed salary should be visible to interviewers, because in most companies they should not, and that is a change to the form rather than a setting. In a group, decide whether a recruiter may open another company's pipeline.

setup.title: Build the scorecard as a survey, not a document
setup.body: A scorecard emailed round the panel as a spreadsheet gives you nothing to report on. The same questions built as a survey attached to the job position put the answers on the applicant, so a hiring manager can compare four candidates against the same criteria. Keep it short. Panels do not complete twenty questions. Six to eight scored questions and one free text box is a form people fill in after every interview.

setup.title: Map the handover to the employee record
setup.body: List, field by field, what has to exist on the employee on day one. Job title, department, manager, work location, start date, contract terms, national identity number, visa or permit reference, bank details for payroll. Much of that is never asked during recruitment, so it has to be collected at offer stage or on a joining form. Decide who fills the gaps and when, or the employee record is created on the start date half empty.

pitfalls.title: Expecting Odoo to read the CV
pitfalls.body: CV digitisation exists as an Enterprise module that sends the document to an external service and consumes in app purchase credits per file. It fills in name, email address and phone number. It does not read the career history, judge whether ten years in the Gulf is relevant, or rank anybody. If the process was designed on the assumption that Odoo shortlists candidates, correct that assumption before the build rather than during user acceptance.

pitfalls.title: Assuming postings go out to job boards on their own
pitfalls.body: Standard Odoo publishes a vacancy on your own website. Pushing the same posting to LinkedIn, Indeed, Bayt or a national portal is integration work, and the harder half is the return path, getting the application and its attachment back into Odoo with the source recorded. Some boards allow a feed, some only manual posting, and some insist on capturing the applicant themselves. Scope each board separately and price only the ones that matter.

pitfalls.title: No retention rule, so the CVs stay forever
pitfalls.body: Odoo does not delete unsuccessful applicants. Two years after go live the database holds thousands of CVs carrying home addresses, dates of birth and passport scans. That is a data protection exposure in the United Kingdom, Germany, France and Turkey, and an information security exposure everywhere else. Agree a retention period, automate an archive or purge past it with a scheduled action, and stop collecting fields that never influenced the decision.

pitfalls.title: Treating the attachment as a searchable database
pitfalls.body: Odoo does not index the text inside a PDF, so no search in the interface will find every candidate who has worked with a particular system. Searching on applicant fields works. Searching inside a thousand attached CVs does not. If a searchable talent pool is a genuine requirement it has to be built from structured fields, tags or skills captured during screening, and somebody has to be paid to enter them.

pitfalls.title: Treating the offer as an internal formality
pitfalls.body: Across much of the Gulf the offer is a regulated document. A Saudi contract is authenticated on Qiwa, and a private sector offer in the United Arab Emirates has to be signed by the candidate before the work permit is applied for. Both are conditional on the employer's quota position. The date somebody can actually start is set by immigration rather than by the hiring manager, so the pipeline needs a stage between accepted and joined.

worksWith: Employees, where the accepted applicant lands with a department, manager, job title and start date
Surveys, which is what an interview form is built from in Community as well as Enterprise
Website, for the public job page, the application form and the translated job description
Calendar, so an interview slot is booked in the interviewer's own diary instead of by email
Sign, an Enterprise app, for the offer letter and contract with a timestamped audit trail
Payroll and the contract record, which need the salary, grade and start date the offer settled
Appraisals, an Enterprise app, for the probation review that closes the loop on a hiring decision
Documents, an Enterprise app, when signed offers and identity papers belong in a controlled workspace

regional.note: Whether an offer can be made at all depends on the Nitaqat band, because the ratio of Saudi to expatriate staff governs the visas the establishment is allowed to hold. Contracts are authenticated on Qiwa and GOSI registration follows the hire, at rates that differ by nationality. Capture nationality and the Qiwa contract reference on the applicant, since both drive everything downstream.

The MOHRE job offer is signed by the candidate before the work permit is applied for, which makes the offer stage a legal step rather than a courtesy. Emiratisation targets apply to companies of fifty or more employees and are measured on skilled roles, with a monthly contribution for each unfilled position. Nationality and skill classification on the applicant feed that count directly.

Labour law is provincial, so a group hiring in Punjab and Sindh works to two sets of standing orders from one database, and the formal appointment letter at hire is a statutory document rather than a template. The CNIC is the identity key for everything that follows, from EOBI and provincial social security registration to the salary account. Collect it at offer stage, not on the first morning.

The gap between offer and joining is the number that matters, since notice periods of thirty to ninety days and candidates holding several offers make dropout normal. Track offered, accepted and joined as separate states. Provident fund and ESIC registration follow the joining date, and a private employer cannot run Aadhaar authentication, so verification goes through a background check vendor.

The SGK employment entry declaration has to be filed at the latest the day before the person starts, so a confirmed start date is a hard deadline for the hire handover rather than a plan. CVs are personal data under KVKK, requiring an information notice and explicit consent. Workplaces with fifty or more staff carry a three percent disabled employee quota filled through İŞKUR.

A right to work check has to be completed before the first day, using a share code for anyone without a British or Irish passport, and the evidence kept for the employment plus two years to hold the statutory excuse. Applicant data sits under UK GDPR, and the regulator expects unsuccessful applicants to be held for a defined period rather than indefinitely.

The works council has a say in hiring under the Works Constitution Act, including the application form and the selection criteria, so the fields on the applicant are a matter for negotiation and not only configuration. The General Equal Treatment Act argues against collecting a photograph, date of birth or marital status, and the short complaint window for rejected candidates sets the retention rule.

Voluntary self identification of race, gender, veteran and disability status has to be collected apart from the hiring decision and kept out of the reviewer's view while remaining available for EEO-1 reporting at one hundred or more employees. Rules on when a criminal record may be asked about vary by state and city, and New York City requires a bias audit before an automated screening tool is used.

faqs.q: Is Odoo Recruitment part of Community or only Enterprise?
faqs.a: The recruitment application is in Odoo Community, along with the website job page, interview forms built on surveys, refusal reasons with templates and the funnel reports. What is Enterprise is the referral programme, CV digitisation, the salary package configurator, Sign for the offer, Documents and Appraisals. A Community deployment can run a complete hiring process without any of those.

faqs.q: Does Odoo read a CV and fill in the applicant automatically?
faqs.a: Only with the Enterprise digitisation module, which sends the document to an external service and uses in app purchase credits per file. It extracts contact details reliably. It does not summarise experience, match a candidate against a job description or produce a shortlist. Screening stays a person reading a CV, and the pipeline is there to record what they decided.

faqs.q: Can Odoo post a vacancy to LinkedIn, Indeed or Bayt?
faqs.a: Not on its own. Odoo publishes the vacancy on your own website and gives you a tracked link per source so applications can be attributed. Posting to an external board and pulling the application back into the pipeline is an integration built per board, and what is possible depends on what that board's API or feed allows. Treat each one as scoped work.

faqs.q: Can a hiring manager see only their own candidates?
faqs.a: Yes. Interviewers form a separate access group and see the applicants assigned to them on a job position rather than the whole pipeline. That makes it reasonable to give line managers a login instead of forwarding CVs by email. Salary fields are visible by default, so decide whether that is acceptable before access is handed out.

faqs.q: What happens in Odoo when we hire someone?
faqs.a: The applicant moves to the stage flagged as hired and an employee record is created from it, carrying name, contact details, department, job position and manager. What does not carry across is everything recruitment never asked for, so joining data, identity numbers, bank details and contract terms have to be gathered at offer stage or on a joining form.

faqs.q: How long can we keep unsuccessful applicants?
faqs.a: Odoo keeps them until you remove them, so the retention period is a decision you make and then automate. Six to twelve months after last contact is a common position in Europe and the United Kingdom, and Turkey requires consent to hold a CV at all. Build a scheduled action that archives past the limit rather than relying on somebody remembering.

faqs.q: Can we send and sign the offer letter from Odoo?
faqs.a: With Enterprise, yes. Sign holds the offer template with role based fields and produces an audit trail with timestamps, and the signed file can be kept against the employee. Enterprise also carries a salary package configurator, but it is built around the Belgian localisation and normally needs reworking before it fits a Gulf or South Asian pay structure.

faqs.q: Do we need Odoo Website to receive applications?
faqs.a: No. An email alias on the job position is enough, and an inbound message becomes an applicant with its attachment kept as the CV. The website module is what gives you a public job page with an application form and a description you can translate. Many employers run both, with the alias catching referrals and direct approaches.
